title: Nodes and subtrees of a binary tree
summary: The root and its branches illustrate the difference between a direct child node and a whole subtree containing that node and all its descendants.
context: This perfect binary tree has 4 levels and 15 nodes, rooted at 1. Values run from 1 to 15 level by level, left to right. Nodes 8 through 15 are leaves with no children. The table lists left and right children for the 7 non-leaf nodes, 1 through 7.
description: An orange area encloses the left subtree of root 1 and a blue area its right subtree. Each area includes the corresponding subtree root and all its descendants.

tables.caption: Left and right children of every non-leaf node in the figure

result: Parent, child, and subtree are relative to the node being considered. Node 1 is the parent of 2 and 3, and 2 is the parent of 4 and 5. The figure labels root 1 “Parent node” because it is the parent of 2 and 3. The root itself has no parent.

frames.title: Nodes and subtrees of a binary tree
frames.explanation: For root 1 the left child is the single node 2 and the right child the single node 3. The left subtree rooted at 2 contains 7 nodes: 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, and 11. The right subtree rooted at 3 also contains 7: 3, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, and 15. A subtree includes its root and all descendants, extending beyond the direct child in this example.
